 Oral Order
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learner APP for the State.

2. The present application has been preferred by the petitioner for quashing the order dated 11.08.2017 passed by the learned C.J.M., Buxar (hereinafter referred to as 'Magistrate') in G.R.
No.24 of 2013 arising out of Buxar (T) P.S. Case No.04 of 2013 wherein the learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence under Section 498A of the Indian Pena Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 against Ravi Prakash Singh (husband of O.P. No.2) and against the petitioner herein, who is cousin (son of maternal uncle) of co- accused Ravi Prakash Singh.
3.

The facts of the case, in brief, as emerging from the Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.33596 of 2018(10) dt.24-03-2026 First Information Report lodged by the informant Vijay Bahadur Singh (O.P. No.3 herein), is that his daughter, Archana Kumari (O.P. No.2), was married to Ravi Prakash Singh on 28.05.2011 in accordance with Hindu rites and rituals.

It is alleged that soon after the marriage, she was subjected to cruelty and harassment by her husband and in-laws on account of Rakesh Kumar Singh vs The State Of Bihar And Ors on 24 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158277901/

sentences.text:
The informant (O.P. No.3) has further alleged that his daughter disclosed that her husband was maintaining an illicit relationship with another woman,
and on account of such circumstances, she was being mentally and physically tortured in her matrimonial home.

It is the case of the prosecution that the said acts of cruelty continued during the subsistence of the matrimonial relationship, whereafter the present F.I.R. came to be instituted on 05.01.2013 giving rise to Buxar (T) P.S. Case No. 04 of 2013, corresponding to G.R. No. 24 of 2013,
under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
4. Upon completion of investigation, the police submitted charge-sheet, and the learned Magistrate,
vide impugned order dated 11.08.2017, took cognizance of the offences against the accused persons including the present petitioner.

Aggrieved by the order of the learned Magistrate, the Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.33596 of 2018(10) dt.24-03-2026 petitioner has preferred the present application for quashing of the impugned order dated 11.08.2017.
5. During the pendency of the present application, certain significant subsequent developments have taken place which have a direct bearing on the controversy involved herein.

It transpires that the matrimonial dispute between the husband, namely Ravi Prakash Singh, and Archana Kumari (O.P.
No.2), has been amicably settled by way of a mutual compromise which is evident from the joint compromise petition dated 05.04.2014 filed before the learned Magistrate.

Pursuant thereto, a joint petition under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act was filed before the learned Principal Judge,
Family Court, Buxar, and the marriage between the parties has already been dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent vide judgment dated 06.09.2014.

It further appears that all disputes,
including the alleged dowry articles, have been settled and returned, and both parties have decided not to pursue the matter any further.
These subsequent developments, having attained finality, are relevant considerations while adjudicating the present application for quashing.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the impugned order taking cognizance is wholly illegal, arbitrary Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.33596 of 2018(10) dt.24-03-2026 and passed without proper application of judicial mind, inasmuch as the petitioner has neither been named in the First Information Report nor any specific overt act has been attributed to him.

It is submitted that the petitioner is a distant relative, having no direct concern with the matrimonial affairs of the husband and wife, and has been falsely implicated in the present case only to harass and humiliate him.

Learned counsel further submits that even during the course of investigation, no material,
either direct or circumstantial, has surfaced so as to connect the petitioner with the alleged offence under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code or under the provisions of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the First Information Report itself suffers from inordinate and unexplained delay of about 18 months from the alleged date of occurrence,
which creates serious doubt about the veracity of the allegations.

Learned counsel submits that during the said period, neither the informant nor the victim lodged any complaint before any authority, which clearly indicates that the allegations have been subsequently concocted.
It is also submitted that the entire criminal proceeding is a fallout of matrimonial discord and has been instituted with an ulterior Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.33596 of 2018(10) dt.24-03-2026 motive to rope in as many family members as possible.

8. Learned counsel next submits that the parties have already amicably settled their dispute by way of a compromise petition and the marriage itself stands dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
He submits that in such circumstances, continuation of the criminal proceeding would be nothing but an abuse of the process of the Court.

It is thus submitted that in view of the settled position of law, where the dispute is essentially matrimonial in nature and has been resolved between the parties, the impugned order as well as the entire criminal proceeding qua the petitioner is fit to be quashed in the interest of justice.

9. Learned APP appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for quashing and submits that the impugned order has been passed on the basis of materials collected during investigation, which disclose prima facie commission of offence.

It is submitted that at the stage of cognizance,
meticulous appreciation of evidence is not required, and since the allegations relate to cruelty and dowry demand, the learned Magistrate has rightly taken cognizance.
It is thus submitted that the present application is fit to be dismissed.

10. Despite valid service of notice upon O.P. Nos. 2 Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.33596 of 2018(10) dt.24-03-2026 and 3, none has chosen to appear on their behalf at the time of hearing of the present application, nor has any counter-affidavit been filed controverting the assertions made in the quashing petition.
Accordingly, this Court proceeds to consider the matter in their absence.

11. In view of the rival submissions advanced on behalf of the parties and upon perusal of the materials available on record, including the First Information Report, the charge- sheet, the impugned order of cognizance, as well as the subsequent developments in the form of compromise and decree of divorce, the issue that falls for consideration before this Court is as to whether the continuance of the criminal proceeding against the present petitioner would amount to an abuse of the process of the Court and whether the impugned order taking cognizance is sustainable in the eyes of law.

12. At the outset, it is well settled that the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is to be exercised sparingly and with great caution, to prevent abuse of the process of the Court or to secure the ends of justice.

It is equally settled that while exercising such jurisdiction, the Court is required to examine whether the uncontroverted allegations made in the complaint and the Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.33596 of 2018(10) dt.24-03-2026 materials collected during investigation disclose the commission of any offence, and where the allegations are manifestly attended with mala fide or do not prima facie constitute any offence, the Court would be justified in quashing the proceeding.

13. It is well settled that although offences under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and allied provisions are non-compoundable, the High Court, in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, may quash criminal proceedings if the dispute is predominantly private and arises out of matrimonial discord, and the parties have settled the matter amicably.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in B.S. Joshi and Ors. v. State of Haryana and Anr., reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675; Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Anr., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303;
Narinder Singh and Ors. v. State of Punjab and Anr., reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466; and Parbatbhai Rakesh Kumar Singh vs The State Of Bihar And Ors on 24 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158277901/
3 Aahir and Ors. v. State of Gujarat and Anr., reported in (2017) 9 SCC 641 has held that in cases having overwhelmingly civil or personal flavour, particularly matrimonial disputes, the High Court may quash the proceedings to secure the ends of justice and to prevent abuse of the process of Court, provided the compromise is genuine and Patna High Court CR. 14. In the recent judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mange Ram v. State of Madhya Pradesh and Anr., reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 1681 has observed as under:
"29.

A three-Judge Bench of this Court in State of M.P. v. Laxmi Narayan, (2019) 5 SCC 688, observed in paragraph 15.5 thereof that while exercising power under Section 482 CrPC to quash the criminal proceedings in respect of non-compoundable offences, which are private in nature and do not have a serious impact on society, on the ground that there is a settlement/compromise between the victim and the offender, it is necessary to consider the antecedents of the accused; the conduct of the accused, namely, whether the accused was absconding and why he was absconding,
how he had managed with the complainant to enter into a compromise, etc. xxx xxx xxx 32.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

In Naushey Ali v. State of U.P., (2025) 4 SCC 78, one of us (Viswanathan, J.)
observed in paragraph 32 that proceeding with the trial, when the parties have amicably resolved the dispute, would be futile and the ends of justice require that the settlement be given effect to by quashing the proceedings.

entities.text: Naushey Ali v. State of U.P., (2025) 4 SCC 78
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It would be a grave abuse of process particularly when the dispute is settled and resolved."
15.
Adverting to the facts of the present case, this Court finds that the petitioner is admittedly not named in the First Information Report and no specific or overt act has been Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.33596 of 2018(10) dt.24-03-2026 attributed to him therein.
The materials on record further indicate that the petitioner is a distant relative of the husband and has no direct concern with the matrimonial affairs of the parties.
Even during the course of investigation, no substantive material has been brought on record to prima facie establish his involvement in the alleged offences.

In such circumstances, the implication of the petitioner appears to be omnibus and general in nature, which does not satisfy the requirements for proceeding against him under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code or the provisions of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
16. This Court further finds that the entire dispute arises out of a matrimonial discord between the husband and wife, which has admittedly been amicably settled between the parties.

The materials on record clearly indicate that a joint compromise petition was filed, all disputes including return of dowry articles have been resolved, and the marriage itself has been dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
In view of such settlement, the substratum of the criminal case no longer survives, and the possibility of conviction in the present case appears to be remote and bleak.

Continuation of the criminal proceeding in such circumstances would amount to sheer abuse of the process of the Court.

4 Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text: It is also pertinent to note that the cumulative effect of the aforesaid circumstances, namely the omnibus nature of allegations, absence of specific role attributed to the petitioner, distant relationship, and subsequent settlement between the parties, leads this Court to the considered view that allowing the criminal proceeding to continue would not serve the ends of justice.

18. Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that the impugned order dated 11.08.2017 passed by the learned C.J.M., Buxar, taking cognizance against the petitioner, cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
The same is hereby quashed.

Consequently, the entire criminal proceeding arising out of Buxar (T) P.S. Case No. 04 of 2013, corresponding to G.R. No. 24 of 2013, stands quashed so far as the present petitioner is concerned.
19.
Accordingly, the present application stands allowed.
